title: Efficacy and Safety of Lebrikizumab in Adults and Adolescents with Face and Neck Atopic Dermatitis
official: A Phase 3b, Multicentre, Randomised, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Parallel-Group Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Lebrikizumab in Adult and Adolescent Participants with Moderate-to-Severe Face and Neck Atopic Dermatitis
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the efficacy of lebrikizumab versus placebo at Week 16 in participants with moderate-to-severe FNAD

interventions.name: Ebglyss 250 mg solution for injection in pre-filled syringe
Solution for injection, containing the same excipients as the respective active lebrikizumab. Identical in appearance to test IMP. Supplied as a sterile PFS NSD.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. Adults and adolescents (aged ≥12 years to <18 years and weighing ≥40 kg) who are candidates for AD systemic therapy.
2. 2. Chronic AD (according to Hanifin and Rajka Criteria [Hanifin 1980]) that has been present for ≥1 year before the Screening visit.
3. 3. At least moderate FNAD with IGA ≥3 at Screening and Day 1/Baseline
4. 4. Overall EASI score ≥12 at Day 1/Baseline with distinct atopic dermatitis lesions in at least one area outside the face and neck.
5. 5. In the Investigator’s judgement, an inadequate response of overall AD to TCS
6. 6. Completed Pruritus NRS eDiary assessment on ≥ 4 of the 7 days immediately preceding the Day 1/Baseline visit.
7. 7. Willing to adhere to general measures aimed at reducing skin dryness and exposure to irritants, including regular use of usual moisturisers, avoidance of known skin irritants and unfamiliar creams, soaps, washing powder or cosmetic products, avoidance of cosmetic treatments or procedures to the skin of the face and neck and implementation of gentle skin care routines (eg, lukewarm baths, patting skin dry).
8. 8. For women of childbearing potential (WOCBP): Agree to remain abstinent (refrain from heterosexual intercourse) or to use a highly effective contraceptive method during the treatment period and for at least 4 weeks or 1 menstrual period after the final dose of IMP.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. Prior treatment with lebrikizumab.
2. 10. Known or suspected history of immunosuppression, including history of invasive opportunistic infections
3. 11. Intention to use any concomitant medication or therapy that is not permitted by this protocol or failure to undergo the required washout period for a particular prohibited medication.
4. 12. Have a known hypersensitivity to any component of lebrikizumab.
5. 13. Uncontrolled chronic disease that might require use of systemic corticosteroids, eg, uncontrolled asthma (defined by a history of ≥2 asthma exacerbations within the last 12 months requiring systemic [oral and/or parenteral] corticosteroid treatment or hospitalisation for >24 hours).
6. 14. Known liver cirrhosis and/or chronic hepatitis of any aetiology or a positive result at Screening for Hepatitis B/C serology.
7. 15. In the Investigator's opinion, any clinically significant abnormalities at the Screening visit.
8. 16. History of malignancy, including mycosis fungoides, within 5 years before the Screening visit, except completely treated in situ carcinoma of the cervix, completely treated and resolved nonmetastatic squamous or basal cell carcinoma of the skin with no evidence of recurrence in the past 12 weeks.
9. 17. Severe concomitant illness(es) that in the Investigator's judgement would adversely affect the participation in the study. Any other medical or psychological condition that in the opinion of the Investigator may suggest a new and/or insufficiently understood disease, may present an unreasonable risk to the study participant because of their participation in this clinical trial, may make participation unreliable, or may interfere with study assessments.
10. 18. Pregnant or breastfeeding women, or women planning to become pregnant or breastfeed during the study.
11. 19. Employee or relative of employees at the study centre or Almirall (or are employees of any third-party involved in the study who require the exclusion of their employees) or participants who are committed to an institution by virtue of an order issued either by the judicial or the administrative authorities.
12. 2. Prior treatment at any time with more than one of the following advanced systemic treatments: Dupilumab, tralokinumab, nemolizumab, or oral JAK inhibitors.
13. 3. Presence of any skin manifestations suggestive of psoriasis including but not limited to nail pitting, scalp, palms, soles or skin folds involvement, as well as personal history of psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis.
14. 4. Presence of dermatological conditions and/or skin signs or symptoms on the face and/or neck that may interfere with study assessments including but not limited to rosacea, flushing, demodicosis, and seborrheic dermatitis.
15. 5. Participants with suspected clinically relevant contact dermatitis of the face and neck region, and participants with a confirmed contact allergen known to exacerbate their atopic dermatitis who cannot commit to allergen avoidance or when allergen avoidance is not possible.
16. 6. Have had any of the following types of infection within 3 months of Screening or develop any of these infections before Day 1/Baseline: Serious (requiring hospitalisation, and/or intravenous [IV] or equivalent oral antibiotic treatment, as per the Investigator's opinion); Opportunistic (as defined by Winthrop et al [Winthrop 2015]). NOTE: Herpes zoster is considered active and ongoing until all vesicles are dry and crusted over: Chronic (duration of symptoms, signs, and/or treatment of 6 weeks or longer); Recurring (including, but not limited to, recurring cellulitis and chronic osteomyelitis). Uncomplicated orolabial or genital herpes simplex infections are not considered exclusionary. Recurrent herpes zoster infection is not exclusionary except when the last episode occurred within 5 years before Day 1/Baseline.
17. 7. Diagnosed active endoparasitic infections or at high risk of these infections.
18. 8. Have an active or acute infection treated with systemic antibiotics, antivirals, antiparasitics, or antifungals within 2 weeks before the Day 1/Baseline visit, or any active skin infection treated with topical antibiotics, anti-virals, anti-parasitics, or anti fungals within one week before the Day 1/Baseline visit.
19. 9. History of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection (including known positive HIV serology in medical history).
